function: Downlink precode-and-compress fronthaul quantization: learned neural codebooks and gradient-based joint bit selection set RU transmit signals minimizing effective interference at UEs, acting as nonlinear precoding (pp. 1, 7-9).
system: Cell-free massive MIMO downlink with multi-antenna RUs on limited fronthaul and multi-antenna UEs (Fig. 7: 4 RUs x16, 4 UEs x4); no RIS; band unstated (pp. 2, 12).
method: Neural-MQ: per-RU fully connected neural codebooks trained with SGD/Adam on channel and symbol samples (unsupervised, sum-EI loss), plus gradient descent with sigmoid annealing for bit selection (pp. 7-10).
data_channel: 3GPP TR 38.901 UMi channels, fixed RUs and random UE positions; codebooks trained on 100 channel realizations; i.i.d. Rayleigh only in small-scale Appendix C (pp. 10-11, 14).
test_conditions: Trained on 100 channel and symbol samples; trained with 1 or 4 UEs, tested with 1-8 UEs; trained at 10 dB, tested -10 to 18 dB (pp. 10, 12-13).
baselines: Non-learned: compress-and-precode (CP) with MMSE precoding, VQ, SMQ, and MQ with Lloyd-Max codebooks [7], infinite-fronthaul linear/nonlinear precoding. Neural-VQ is the authors' variant; no earlier learned method (pp. 10-11, 14).
metrics: Sum spectral efficiency (bit/s/Hz), average 16-QAM symbol error rate, spectral efficiency versus computational complexity, sum effective interference (pp. 10-15).
complexity: Complexity orders in Table I, neural-MQ linear in the sum fronthaul rate; flops per channel use at DU and RU in Tables II-III (pp. 5, 9, 14).
q1_support: p. 11, Fig. 6 caption: "The channel is generated by following 3GPP urban micro (UMi) models [21]"; [21] is 3GPP TR 38.901 (p. 15).
q2_support: p. 12: "training assumes a number N of UEs equal to either 1 or 4, while testing for N = 1, ..., 8 UEs" (Fig. 9).
q3_support: p. 10: compared "against conventional PC schemes, i.e., VQ (Sec. II-D) [7], SMQ (Sec. III-C), and MQ" and CP; the only other neural scheme, neural-VQ, "follows the same procedure as in neural-MQ" (p. 14). No earlier learned baseline.
q4_support: p. 9: neural-MQ "would require computational complexity of the order O(2I · ...)" which "grows linearly with fronthaul sum-rate"; p. 14, Table II: "Computational complexity at DU per channel use" in flops.
q5_support: p. 10, footnote 1: "Code is available at https://github.com/kclip/scalable-MQ."
notes: Area 3 is a judgment call for the reviewer: neural-MQ quantizes precoded baseband signals for the fronthaul, with neural codebooks at the RUs and gradient-based bit selection at the DU that minimizes effective interference (MSE) at the UEs; the paper ties it to nonlinear precoding, and it beats infinite-fronthaul linear precoding (pp. 11-12). I treated it as transmit-signal (precoding) design; if fronthaul compression is read as outside the seven areas, the reason would be 'function' (p. 1). The precoder W itself is MMSE, not learned (p. 10), and the other proposal, alpha-PMQ, is not learned. q3: VQ, SMQ, and MQ of [7] use Lloyd-Max (K-means) codebooks trained on data (p. 5), which the paper calls 'conventional PC schemes' (p. 10), so I counted them as non-learned; neural-VQ (Appendix A) is the authors' variant. If the reviewer counts the K-means codebooks of [7] (same senior author) as an earlier learned method, q3 would be 1. q1: the 100 training channel realizations (p. 10) are not described separately; every figure caption states channels follow 3GPP UMi [21].
